episodes.193186: Very hot temperatures combined with a weak mid-level short wave trough creating isolated thunderstorms late in the afternoon into the evening of the 14th. A very deeply mixed boundary layer led to a dry sub-cloud layer and high based thunderstorms. A couple of these thunderstorms produced severe wind gusts near Plains (Yoakum County) and Olton (Lamb County).
episodes.193188: Severe thunderstorms produced numerous reports of damaging winds during the evening of August 14th.  Many of the damage reports were likely due to what are called wet downbursts of locally damaging winds of 65 to 80 mph.  A supercell thunderstorm also developed near a warm frontal boundary and did produce a brief tornado based on photos however no damage was reported.
episodes.193240: Another afternoon of isolated thunderstorms developed under very hot conditions and an approaching weak short wave trough. A cold front moved through the Texas Panhandle and stalled out from the western South Plains into the extreme southeastern Texas Panhandle. Thunderstorms initially developed along this boundary but with very dry sub-cloud layers, these thunderstorms were efficient strong wind producers. Several storms generated severe wind gusts including a wet microburst near Flomot (Motley County) producing a wind gust of 90 mph.
episodes.193267: Strong wind gusts reported over eastern Laramie County early in the evening on the 14th as a surging outflow from a convective line of storms moving across southeast Wyoming into the Nebraska panhandle.
episodes.193276: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a boundary over northeast Oklahoma and southeast Kansas during the afternoon hours on August 15, 2024. As the boundary progressed, additional thunderstorms developed just north of and along Interstate 44, with hail sizes ranging between quarter size and golf ball size in Dallas and Webster counties, and up to 3.25 inches in Camden County. Additionally, Damaging winds resulted in multiple reports of tree and powerline damage, with 60 mph winds reported in Greene County and 65 mph winds in Miller County. These storms remained over the Missouri Ozarks into the early morning of August 16, 2024, resulting in additional flooding concerns.
episodes.193515: A round of afternoon thunderstorms associated with a cold front moved from north to south during the afternoon and evening bringing wind damage and severe hail to eastern Massachusetts. There was also localized flash flooding in Fall River.
episodes.193516: A round of afternoon thunderstorms associated with a cold front moved from north to south during the afternoon and evening bringing wind damage and severe hail to eastern Massachusetts. There was also localized flash flooding in MA and RI. In CT one storm produced severe hail.
episodes.193551: A round of afternoon thunderstorms associated with a cold front moved from north to south during the afternoon and evening bringing flash flooding to portions of coastal Rhode Island. There was also wind damage and severe hail in eastern Massachusetts.
episodes.193590: Discrete supercells developed over southeast Missouri during the afternoon of August 15th. These thunderstorms moved east into Illinois where one cell produced minor wind damage in far southern Randolph County.
episodes.193818: Strong wind gusts reported over Cheyenne County near Sidney early in the evening on the 14th as an outflow boundary accelerated away from a decaying convective line of storms.
episodes.194250: A southwesterly flow aloft combined with ample surface heating to result in deep inverted-V soundings. Thunderstorms that formed along the Rocky Mountain Front moved eastward through the afternoon and early evening, resulting in a few strong wind gusts. This episode will also contain a gust from the Dillon area on the 15th from strong outflow. Deep inverted-V soundings supported this stronger gust.
episodes.194423: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over eastern Fall River County, producing strong wind gusts in the Hot Springs area.
episodes.194430: Scattered convection developed across the High Plains during the afternoon into early evening of the 15th. A few generally decaying thunderstorms moved into portions of far northern Oklahoma, producing gusty winds. A damaging downburst wind event was observed near the community of Buffalo, Oklahoma.
episodes.194431: As a closed upper system strengthened and moved towards the Corn Belt, a trailing cold front pushed into portions of western and central Oklahoma during the afternoon and evening of the 15th. Multiple areas of convective activity emerged near and ahead of this feature, coincident with strong surface heating. Marginal deep-layer wind shear promoted generally disorganized (multi-cell) storm modes. In addition to wind damage (downburst) events, a few reports of large hail were also received.
episodes.195001: A line of thunderstorms moved through northwestern North Dakota during the late afternoon and evening hours. One storm became severe, producing 60 mph wind gusts near Watford City in McKenzie County.
episodes.195118: A few thunderstorms developed during the evening along a weak surface trough with up to 1500 J/kg MLCAPE. Weak deep-layer shear limited organization potential, with merging cold pools quickly reducing the intensity of storms along the line.
episodes.195329: A weak surface boundary moving across South Florida brought ample instability, lift, and moisture advection to provide conditions prime for afternoon convection on August 15th. Numerous showers and thunderstorms brough the threat for hazards such as heavy downpours and gusty winds.
episodes.195330: Upper air analysis on the morning of August 14th showed troughing over the Pacific Northwest and a shortwave ridge with its axis positioned over the upper Mississippi River Valley. Divergence aloft over the central Great Plains developed two areas of low pressure at the surface as analyzed by Weather Prediction Center surface analysis maps. One low pressure was centered over South Dakota, the other in northwest Kansas. The two low pressures were connected by a stationary front, and a warm front extended southeast out of the southern low pressure into the lower Mississippi river Valley. By the afternoon hours, convection developed along and on the cool side of this warm front, resulting in scattered strong to severe thunderstorms across much of southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa. Though both states saw severe thunderstorm warnings, the only severe weather reports came out of Nebraska where a funnel cloud, quarter sized hail, and wind gust of 58 miles per hour were all reported. Training thunderstorms in the Omaha metro later that night resulted in isolated pockets of urban flash flooding in Douglas County south of Interstate 80.
episodes.195334: In the late evening hours, a line of storms brought us several severe wind gusts to portions of far eastern Kansas.
episodes.195335: In the late evening hours, a line of storms brought a severe wind gust to Platte County.
episodes.195339: As Hurricane Ernesto moved farther away from the region, it promoted a southeasterly wind flow across the islands, creating favorable weather conditions for waterspout formation.
episodes.195413: Isolated late afternoon storms morphed into a fairly small mesoscale convective system that surged southeastward through Southwestern Illinois. MLCAPE was 3000 J/kg, decreasing to 2000 J/kg for the evening. Effective bulk shear was 30 kts. A localized swath of significant wind damage occurred in portions of Southwestern Illinois with the most concentrated area of wind damage near Karnak. Other areas receiving wind damage were Gorham, Dongola, Cypress, and Joppa.
episodes.195436: A line of severe storms produced damaging winds across much of central and southcentral Kansas during the evening and nighttime hours of August 14th. There were several reports of structural damage with wind gusts up to 80 mph reported for the strongest of these storms. Schools in the towns of Douglass and Sedgwick were cancelled the following day due to damage caused by these storms. These storms also brought frequent cloud-to-ground lightning, and a person was injured by a nearby lightning strike.
episodes.195437: An isolated storm developed over the Oklahoma-Kansas state line and produced quarter sized hail over far southeast Sumner County during the early evening of August 15.
episodes.195458: A fairly typical summertime upper level pattern was in place with strong high pressure centered well west of the local area. That put southern Louisiana and Mississippi on the eastern periphery of this ridge in a region of northwestern upper level flow. That setup is often conducive for strong to severe thunderstorm development and what took place on August 14th as severe storms tracked across the local coastal waters.
episodes.195460: A fairly typical summertime upper level pattern was in place with strong high pressure centered well west of the local area. That put southern Louisiana on the eastern periphery of this ridge in a region of northwestern upper level flow. That setup is often conducive for strong to severe thunderstorm development and what took place on August 15th. Thunderstorms initially developed in central Mississippi early afternoon. As the storms traveled southwestward, they moved into an environment with ample instability from strong daytime heating. The resultant cluster of storms organized into a line of strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.195461: A fairly typical summertime upper level pattern was in place with strong high pressure centered well west of the local area. That put southern Louisiana on the eastern periphery of this ridge in a region of northwestern upper level flow. That setup is often conducive for strong to severe thunderstorm development and what took place on August 15th. Thunderstorms initially developed in central Mississippi early afternoon. As the storms traveled southwestward, they moved into an environment with ample instability from strong daytime heating. The resultant cluster of storms organized into a line of strong to severe thunderstorms.
episodes.195515: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the evening of the 15th, ahead of an approaching cold front. The atmosphere ahead of the cold front became very unstable during the afternoon and early evening across eastern Oklahoma, which supported severe thunderstorms that produced large hail up to half dollar size and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.195712: After morning convection across much of Iowa, additional convection occurred during the late afternoon to evening, with the majority of activity over southern Iowa. Conditions were suitable for storm development, which included 35-45 knots of 0-6 km bulk shear and 2000-3000+ J/kg of MLCAPE, with a shortwave pushing across the area. Most notable was the near severe hail that occurred in Poweshiek county from one rather strong cell, with reported hail at 0.75 inches.
episodes.195778: An upper level disturbance overhead resulted in the development of isolated showers and thunderstorms on August 15, 2024 within the Hudson Valley region of eastern New York. Some of these storms reached severe limits downing trees and wires and also producing hail in excess of 1 inch in diameter.
episodes.195852: A weak surface boundary moving across South Florida brought ample instability, lift, and moisture advection to provide conditions prime for afternoon convection on August 15th. Numerous showers and thunderstorms brough the threat for hazards such as heavy downpours, gusty winds, and localized flooding with any slow moving storms.
episodes.196090: Several reports of severe weather received.
episodes.196149: The area was situated on the western edge of an upper level low as it spun over the Canadian Maritimes. An embedded shortwave rotated around the low and helped spark thunderstorms in a very unstable environment. One of these storms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.196213: Instability storms developed on the evening of August 14th across the higher terrain of the Western Maine Mountains, especially across Somerset County.  Storms had limited shear, but a few were still strong enough to produce damaging and isolated large hail.  Overall coverage remained low and only impacted a few towns.
episodes.196214: An upper-level low over the Canadian Maritimes brought a strong jet overhead which provided strong shear to the state of New Hampshire on the afternoon of August 15th.  This allowed for strong to severe thunderstorms to develop from Central New Hampshire that quickly traveled southward into Southern New Hampshire, bringing with it large hail and damaging winds.
episodes.196341: Afternoon thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce a funnel cloud near Shell Creek in Charlotte County.
